mainTopic: נבוזראדן's destruction of ירושלים and his conversion, enemies whose descendants joined the Torah world, how עמון ומואב urged נבוכדנצר to attack, and the start of the discussion about משיח
overview: The גמרא first asks how נבוזראדן could stand before the king of Babylon in ירושלים when נבוכדנצר was far away in רבלה, and two אמוראים explain that he acted as if his master were there. Then רבא tells how ירושלים fell: one gate wore out 300 loads of iron axes, until a בת קול said the time had come, and a tap from the last axe opened it. When נבוזראדן burned the היכל and grew proud, a בת קול told him he had only ground flour that was already ground. He found the blood of the murdered נביא זכריה boiling, killed 940,000 people trying to calm it, and was so shaken that he did תשובה and converted. A ברייתא adds that descendants of סיסרא, סנחריב (שמעיה ואבטליון) and המן learned Torah, but the angels blocked ה׳'s wish to accept נבוכדנצר's descendants. Next, עולא tells how עמון ומואב convinced a fearful נבוכדנצר to attack, answering each of his excuses with a פסוק. Finally רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק when 'בר נפלי', meaning משיח, will come, and begins quoting a פסוק that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Was נבוכדנצר really in ירושלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that נבוכדנצר was in ירושלים. A פסוק shows he stayed in רבלה, which רבי אבהו says is אנטוכיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did נבוכדנצר actually go up to ירושלים? The פסוק says that צדקיהו was brought up to the king of Babylon at רבלה, and רבי אבהו says רבלה is אנטוכיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning the earlier description of נבוזראדן standing before the king of Babylon in ירושלים. Another פסוק shows that נבוכדנצר was far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא spoke of נבוזראדן standing "before the king of Babylon" at ירושלים. Here the גמרא brings a פסוק showing that צדקיהו had to be brought to the king at רבלה. רבי אבהו identifies רבלה as אנטוכיא, so נבוכדנצר was not in ירושלים at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really go up? (a challenging question)
But isn't it written? (brings a פסוק as a challenge)
To רבלה, where the king of Babylon was
אנטוכיא, a city far north of ירושלים

phrases.english: And did Nebuchadnezzar go up to Jerusalem?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וַיַּעֲלוּ אֹתוֹ אֶל מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל רִבְלָתָה״,
phrases.english: But isn't it written: "And they brought him up to the king of Babylon, to Riblah,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 25:6. "Him" is צדקיהו, the captured king of יהודה.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Abbahu said: This is Antioch!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סְלֵיק נְבוּכַד נֶצַּר לִירוּשָׁלַיִם? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the earlier פסוק about נבוזראדן standing before the king in ירושלים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that נבוכדנצר was present in ירושלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק places נבוכדנצר in רבלה, which is אנטוכיא, so he could not have been in ירושלים.

steps.title: Two explanations of standing before an absent king
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב יצחק בר אבודימי explain how נבוזראדן could be standing before a king who was not there. In one view, an image of נבוכדנצר was carved on his chariot. In the other, he feared his master so much that he always acted as if he stood before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said: a picture of נבוכדנצר was carved on נבוזראדן's chariot. The other said: נבוזראדן was so afraid of נבוכדנצר that it was as if he were always standing in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question by explaining that the "standing before" was not physical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither answer claims that נבוכדנצר was in ירושלים, so the פסוק about רבלה stays true. One answer points to a physical reminder, an image on the chariot. The other answer is about feeling: his fear and respect made him behave as if his master were present.

keyTerms.meaning: One said... and one said (two אמוראים, without saying who said which)

steps.whatToRemember: נבוזראדן showed his master such honor that he acted as though נבוכדנצר were always in front of him, even from far away.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי,
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda and Rav Yitzḥak bar Avudimi disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: דְּמוּת דְּיוֹקְנוֹ הָיְתָה חֲקוּקָה לוֹ
phrases.english: One says: An image of his likeness was engraved for him
phrases.notes: The image is of נבוכדנצר, and it was carved for נבוזראדן to see.

phrases.english: on his chariot,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵימָה יְתֵירָה הָיְתָה לוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ
phrases.english: and one says: He had extreme fear of him,
and it was as if he were standing before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: "standing before" is symbolic, not physical.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to mean that נבוכדנצר was physically present in ירושלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: נבוזראדן acted as if he were before his master, either because of a carved image or because of his intense fear.

steps.title: Three hundred loads of axes used up on one gate
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that נבוכדנצר sent 300 mule-loads of iron-cutting axes to נבוזראדן, and every one was used up on a single gate of ירושלים. The source is a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: נבוכדנצר sent נבוזראדן 300 mules loaded with iron axes strong enough to cut iron. One gate of ירושלים wore out all of them, as the פסוק says: "They pound its doors together with hatchet and hammers."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story from רבא about how ירושלים fell. It starts by showing how hard it was to break in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These were the strongest tools there were, axes that could cut iron, and in huge numbers. Even so, one gate swallowed them all. The point is that the city could not be taken by human strength alone.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Three hundred mules laden
with iron axes that cut through iron
Nebuchadnezzar sent to Nebuzaradan.
One gate of Jerusalem swallowed all of them,
phrases.notes: Literally "swallowed." He means the gate wore out every single axe.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "They pound its carved doors together with hatchet and hammers."
phrases.notes: תהלים 74:6

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: טְעוֹן תְּלָת מְאָה כּוּדַנְיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the honor נבוזראדן gave his master to the story of the destruction itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gate of ירושלים resisted 300 loads of iron-cutting axes.

steps.title: נבוזראדן fears סנחריב's fate
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן wants to retreat, because he is afraid of ending up like סנחריב, whose army was destroyed at ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He wanted to go back. He said: I'm afraid they will do to me what they did to סנחריב.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: after failing at the gate, נבוזראדן gets scared and thinks about turning back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבוזראדן remembers that סנחריב attacked ירושלים and was struck down from Heaven. His failure at the gate makes him think the same protection is still in place.

keyTerms.meaning: סנחריב, the Assyrian king whose army fell at ירושלים

phrases.english: He wanted to turn back; he said:
I am afraid that they will do to me
just as they did to Sennacherib.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how נבוזראדן reacted to the failure at the gate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבוזראדן was afraid to continue because of what happened to סנחריב.

steps.title: A Heavenly voice says the time has come
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול tells נבוזראדן to leap ahead, because the time has come for the בית המקדש to be destroyed. With his last axe he taps the gate with the blunt end, and it opens. The source is a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A voice came out and said: "Leaper son of a leaper, נבוזראדן, leap! The time has come for the בית המקדש to be destroyed and the היכל to burn." He had one axe left. He hit the gate with its back end and it opened, as the פסוק says: "He was known as one who lifts axes up into a thicket of trees."
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven gives permission, and suddenly the gate that defeated 300 loads of axes opens with one light tap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the iron-cutting axes failed. Now even the blunt end of one leftover axe works. This shows that what changed was Heaven's timing, not נבוזראדן's strength.

keyTerms.meaning: The back, blunt end of the axe

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think נבוזראדן found a better technique. The גמרא's point is that the gate opened only because Heaven decided it was time.

phrases.english: A voice emerged and said:
"Leaper, son of a leaper, Nebuzaradan, leap!
For the time has arrived for the Temple to be destroyed
and the Sanctuary to be burned."
One axe remained for him.
He came and struck it with the back end, and it opened,
as it is stated: "He became known as one who brings upward
axes into a thicket of trees."
phrases.notes: תהלים 74:5

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא קָלָא וְאָמַר: שָׁוַור בַּר שָׁוַור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers נבוזראדן's fear from step 4 and reverses the failure from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gate opened only when Heaven declared that the time for the destruction had come.

steps.title: The Sanctuary rises and is pressed down from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן kills his way up to the היכל and sets it on fire. The היכל rises up, and it is trampled down from Heaven. The source is a פסוק in איכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He kept killing as he went, until he reached the היכל. He set it on fire. The היכל rose up. They trod it down from Heaven, as the פסוק says: "ה׳ has trodden the maiden daughter of יהודה like a winepress."
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches the burning of the היכל, and once again Heaven is the one acting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היכל rising shows it would not be destroyed by a human. It went down only because Heaven pushed it down. The פסוק in איכה, which says ה׳ "trod" it, is the source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: He lit a fire in it

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָטֵיל וְאָזֵל, עַד דִּמְטָא לְהֵיכְלָא.
phrases.english: He went on killing, until he reached the Sanctuary.
He lit a fire in it.
The Sanctuary rose up.
They trod upon it from Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״גַּת דָּרַךְ ה׳ לִבְתוּלַת בַּת יְהוּדָה״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: "The Lord has trodden the virgin daughter of Judah as a winepress."
phrases.notes: איכה 1:15

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה קָטֵיל וְאָזֵל, עַד דִּמְטָא לְהֵיכְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the gate opens.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The היכל was brought down by Heaven, not by נבוזראדן.

steps.title: You killed a dead nation and burned a burned Sanctuary
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן becomes proud. A בת קול tells him he only killed a nation that was already dead, burned a היכל that was already burned, and ground flour that was already ground. The source is a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He became proud. A בת קול came out and told him: You killed a nation that was already killed, you burned a היכל that was already burned, you ground flour that was already ground, as the פסוק says: "Take millstones and grind flour; uncover your locks, lift your skirt, bare your leg, cross rivers."
steps.whatsHappening: נבוזראדן takes credit for the destruction, and Heaven tells him he really did nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three pictures (killing the dead, burning the burned, grinding flour) all say the same thing. The destruction had already been decided and carried out by Heaven, and נבוזראדן only finished it off. The פסוק is said to בבל, which was told to grind flour.

phrases.english: He became proud.
A Divine Voice emerged and said to him:
You killed a nation that was already killed,
you burned a Sanctuary that was already burned,
you ground flour that was already ground,
as it is stated: "Take millstones and grind flour;
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 47:2. The פסוק is talking to בבל.

phrases.english: uncover your locks, lift up the train,
uncover the leg, pass over rivers."

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא זִיחָא דַּעְתֵּיהּ. נְפַקָא בַּת קָלָא וַאֲמַרָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Heaven responds to נבוזראדן's pride after he burned the היכל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבוזראדן's role in the destruction was meaningless, because Heaven had already done it.

steps.title: Flour, not wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the exact word in the פסוק. It says to grind "קמח" (flour), not "חטים" (wheat), which shows that the job was already done before בבל came.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק does not say "wheat," only "flour."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly where in the פסוק it learned "you ground flour that was already ground."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you grind wheat into flour. Telling someone to grind flour means grinding something that is already ground. So בבל added nothing real to the destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not say X, but rather Y (learning from an exact word choice)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole story teaches one idea: ירושלים and the בית המקדש fell only because Heaven decreed it. נבוזראדן had no power of his own, and his pride was empty.

phrases.english: "Wheat" is not stated, but rather "flour."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 7 proves what the בת קול said.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Grinding flour, not wheat, shows that the destruction was already complete from Heaven before נבוזראדן acted.

steps.title: נבוזראדן finds blood that will not stop boiling
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן sees boiling blood in the בית המקדש. The כהנים claim it is blood of קרבנות. He tests their claim, finds it false, and threatens them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He saw the blood of זכריה boiling. He asked them, 'What is this?' They said, 'It is blood of offerings that was spilled.' He said, 'Bring animals and I will check whether the blood is the same.' He slaughtered them, and the blood was not the same. He said, 'Tell me the truth, or I will tear your flesh with iron combs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on inside the בית המקדש. נבוזראדן finds strange boiling blood and pushes the כהנים to tell him what it really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים first try to hide the truth by saying it is ordinary blood from קרבנות. נבוזראדן checks it himself, and the animal blood does not boil, so he knows they lied. His threat forces them to reveal the real story in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: I will test, I will check
an iron comb, used to tear flesh

steps.confusionAlert: The זכריה here is the כהן and נביא who was killed in the בית המקדש. He is not the נביא זכריה of תרי עשר.

phrases.english: He saw the blood of Zechariah
phrases.notes: This is the זכריה who was killed in the בית המקדש. See דברי הימים ב 24:20–22.

phrases.english: that was boiling.
He said to them: What is this?
They said to him: It is the blood of offerings
that was spilled.
He said to them: Bring animals, and I will test
phrases.notes: The word 'animals' is not written, but the next line shows that is what he means.

phrases.english: whether the bloods are alike.
He slaughtered them, and they were not alike.
He said to them: Reveal it to me,
and if not, I will comb your flesh
with an iron comb.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזָא דְּמֵיהּ דִּזְכַרְיָה דַּהֲוָה קָא רָתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of נבוזראדן after he entered and burned the היכל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood of זכריה was still boiling. The כהנים' cover story failed when נבוזראדן tested it.

steps.title: The כהנים reveal the truth, and נבוזראדן kills masses of people
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים admit the blood belongs to a כהן and נביא whom they killed. נבוזראדן tries to calm it by killing Sages, schoolchildren, and young כהנים, 940,000 people in all, but it keeps boiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said, 'This is the blood of a כהן and נביא who warned Israel about the destruction of ירושלים, and they killed him.' He said, 'I will calm it.' He brought the Sages and killed them over it, and it did not rest. He brought schoolchildren and killed them over it, and it did not rest. He brought young כהנים and killed them over it, and it did not rest. He killed 940,000 people over it, and it still did not rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The כהנים tell the true story behind the blood. נבוזראדן tries to quiet it by killing more and more groups of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we learn why the blood boils: an innocent נביא was murdered for warning about the חורבן. The same line repeats again and again, 'he killed over it, and it did not rest,' to show that all this killing still does not quiet the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: I will appease, I will calm

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הַאי כֹּהֵן וְנָבִיא הוּא,
phrases.english: They said to him: This is the blood of a priest and a prophet,
who prophesied to Israel
about the destruction of Jerusalem, and they killed him.
He said to them: I will calm it.

phrases.aramaic: אַיְיתִי רַבָּנַן, קָטֵיל עִילָּוֵיהּ, וְלָא נָח.
phrases.english: He brought the Sages and killed them over it, and it did not rest.
He brought the schoolchildren,
killed them over it, and it did not rest.

phrases.aramaic: אַיְיתִי פִּרְחֵי כְהוּנָּה, קָטֵיל עִילָּוֵיהּ, וְלָא נָח.
phrases.english: He brought young priests and killed them over it, and it did not rest.
Until he had killed over it
ninety-four times ten thousand, and it did not rest.
phrases.notes: A רִיבּוֹא is 10,000, so this is 940,000 people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הַאי כֹּהֵן וְנָבִיא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The כהנים give in to the threat of Step 9 and reveal the truth. נבוזראדן then acts on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood was that of a murdered כהן and נביא. Even 940,000 deaths could not quiet it.

steps.title: נבוזראדן speaks to זכריה, and the blood rests
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן speaks directly to זכריה and asks whether he wants every last person killed. The blood immediately stops boiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came close to it and said, 'זכריה, זכריה, I have destroyed the best of them. Do you want me to kill all of them?' Right away it rested.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of killing more people, נבוזראדן speaks to זכריה himself, and the boiling stops at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killing did not calm the blood, but this plea did. The word מִיָּד shows that the blood rested the moment נבוזראדן asked whether זכריה wanted everyone destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: is it pleasing to you, do you want

phrases.english: He approached it and said: Zechariah, Zechariah,
the best among them I have destroyed.
Do you want me to kill all of them?
Immediately it rested.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The killing in Step 10 failed. Here a direct plea succeeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood rested only when נבוזראדן appealed to זכריה directly.

steps.title: נבוזראדן does תשובה and converts
steps.stepSummary: נבוזראדן reasons that if one murder needed so much punishment, his own mass killing must be far worse. He deserts, sends a will home, and converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought about doing תשובה. He said, 'If they killed only one person and it took all this, what will happen to me?' He ran away, sent his will to his family, and became a גר.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוזראדן is shaken by what he has seen. He compares himself to the killers of זכריה and decides to change his life completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning moves from the smaller case to the bigger one: one murder brought this much punishment, so his hundreds of thousands of killings are much worse. Because of this he gives up everything, his army and his home, and becomes a גר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'that man', a polite way of saying 'me'

steps.whatToRemember: The enemy general who destroyed the בית המקדש was so shaken by the punishment for one murder that he did תשובה and converted.

phrases.english: He thought about repentance in his mind and said:
If they, who destroyed
only one soul, needed all this,
that man, what will become of him?
phrases.notes: 'That man' is a polite way of talking about himself.

phrases.english: He fled, sent a will to his household, and converted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After seeing the blood rest, נבוזראדן draws a conclusion about himself.

steps.title: A ברייתא on converts and on enemies' descendants who learned Torah
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says נעמן was only a גר תושב, while נבוזראדן was a full גר צדק. It adds that descendants of סיסרא and סנחריב became Torah scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: נעמן was a גר תושב. נבוזראדן was a גר צדק. Some descendants of סיסרא learned Torah in ירושלים. Some descendants of סנחריב taught Torah in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the story it just told. It confirms that נבוזראדן became a full convert, and it lists other enemies of Israel whose families joined the Torah world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares two non-Jews. נעמן only gave up עבודה זרה, which makes him a גר תושב. נבוזראדן converted fully, which makes him a גר צדק. It then goes further: even the descendants of סיסרא and סנחריב became Torah scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-Jew who gives up עבודה זרה but does not fully convert

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two types of גר. A גר תושב is not Jewish. A גר צדק is fully Jewish.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נַעֲמָן - גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב הָיָה,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: Naaman was a resident alien (ger toshav);
Nebuzaradan was a righteous convert.
Some of the descendants of Sisera
learned Torah in Jerusalem;
some of the descendants of Sennacherib
taught Torah in public.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נַעֲמָן - גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the conversion of Step 12 and widens the topic to other enemies and their descendants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבוזראדן was a full גר צדק. Descendants of סיסרא and סנחריב became Torah scholars.

steps.title: Who were the descendants of סנחריב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the descendants of סנחריב were who taught Torah in public.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who were they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to identify the people the ברייתא mentioned. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not name the descendants of סנחריב who taught Torah. The גמרא wants to know exactly who they were.

phrases.english: And who are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the names of the people mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of סנחריב's descendants who taught Torah in public.

steps.title: They were שמעיה ואבטליון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the descendants of סנחריב who taught Torah in public were שמעיה ואבטליון.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעיה ואבטליון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by naming the two great teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The descendants of the king who attacked ירושלים became famous teachers of Torah. This fits the theme of this section: enemies of Israel whose families joined the Jewish people.
steps.whatToRemember: The great teachers שמעיה ואבטליון descended from סנחריב, the enemy king who attacked ירושלים.

phrases.english: Shemaya and Avtalyon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The descendants of סנחריב who taught Torah in public were שמעיה ואבטליון.

steps.title: המן's descendants learned Torah in בני ברק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: some descendants of המן learned Torah in בני ברק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of המן's descendants learned Torah in בני ברק.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 13 keeps going and adds another enemy whose descendants became Torah learners: המן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13–15 named descendants of סיסרא and סנחריב who became Torah scholars. Now המן is added to the same list. The point is that even the families of Israel's worst enemies can join the Torah world.

keyTerms.meaning: The villain of the Purim story
A town in ארץ ישראל known for Torah learning

phrases.english: Among the descendants of Haman
were those who learned Torah in Bnei Brak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of enemies whose descendants became Torah scholars.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המן's descendants learned Torah in בני ברק.

steps.title: ה׳ wanted to bring in נבוכדנצר's descendants too
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to bring even the descendants of נבוכדנצר under the wings of the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even with the descendants of that wicked man, הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to bring them in under the wings of the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says that ה׳ wanted to let even נבוכדנצר's descendants convert. This sets up the angels' protest in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבוכדנצר destroyed the בית המקדש, so he is the hardest case of all. The words 'and even' show that this goes further than המן, סיסרא and סנחריב.

keyTerms.meaning: That wicked man, here meaning נבוכדנצר
Under the wings of the Divine Presence, meaning becoming a גר

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
phrases.english: And even among the descendants of that wicked man
phrases.notes: 'That wicked man' is נבוכדנצר, who destroyed the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to bring them under the wings of the Divine Presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף מִבְּנֵי בָּנָיו שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the list to its most extreme case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ wanted to accept even נבוכדנצר's descendants.

steps.title: The angels protest
steps.stepSummary: The מלאכי השרת object: should the one who destroyed Your House be brought under the שכינה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The ministering angels said to ה׳: Master of the world, the one who destroyed Your House and burned Your Sanctuary, You will bring him under the wings of the שכינה?
steps.whatsHappening: The angels protest ה׳'s wish to accept נבוכדנצר's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their argument is about what נבוכדנצר did: he destroyed and burned the בית המקדש. Inside the story the question works like a challenge, and the next step shows it was accepted.

phrases.english: The ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
the one who destroyed Your House
and burned Your Sanctuary,
You will bring under the wings of the Divine Presence?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to ה׳'s wish in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The angels argue that the destroyer of the מקדש should not be accepted.

steps.title: A verse describes the failed healing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects this to the פסוק 'We healed Babylon, but she was not healed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what is written: 'We have healed Babylon, but she is not healed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from ירמיה that matches the story: an attempt to heal Babylon that did not succeed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'We tried to heal' matches ה׳'s wish to bring them in. 'She was not healed' matches that it did not happen because of the angels' protest. The next two steps argue about what exactly the פסוק refers to.

phrases.english: That is what is written:
"We have healed Babylon, but she is not healed."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 51:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק that matches the story.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳'s wish to accept נבוכדנצר's descendants was not carried out.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיה נא:ט, 'רפינו את בבל ולא נרפתה'

steps.title: עולא: the פסוק is about נבוכדנצר
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the פסוק refers to נבוכדנצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: This is נבוכדנצר.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא says the 'Babylon' that could not be healed is נבוכדנצר himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא reads the פסוק the same way as the story just told: the 'healing' was the attempt to bring נבוכדנצר's family close. This is the first of two readings.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who traveled between ארץ ישראל and בבל
King of Babylon who destroyed the first בית המקדש

phrases.english: Ulla said: This is Nebuchadnezzar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains whom the פסוק refers to.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: the rivers of Babylon
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says the פסוק refers to the salty rivers of Babylon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: These are the rivers of Babylon. And translate it as: the salty, bitter rivers of the Babylonians.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives a different reading: the פסוק is about Babylon's rivers, not about a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his reading, the 'healing' that did not work is about the bad, salty water that stayed bad. So according to him, this פסוק is not proof for the story about נבוכדנצר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
These are the rivers of Babylon,
and translate it as:
the salty, bitter streams of the Babylonians.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: אֵלּוּ נַהֲרוֹת בָּבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with עולא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק refers to Babylon's salty rivers.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists enemies whose descendants joined Torah life, but נבוכדנצר's family was blocked. עולא connects the פסוק in ירמיה to נבוכדנצר; רבי שמואל בר נחמני says it is about rivers.

steps.title: עמון ומואב invite נבוכדנצר to attack
steps.stepSummary: עולא: עמון ומואב, bad neighbors of ירושלים, heard the prophecies of destruction and told נבוכדנצר to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: עמון ומואב were bad neighbors of ירושלים. When they heard the נביאים prophesying the destruction of ירושלים, they sent to נבוכדנצר: Go out and come.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins about how the חורבן started. עמון ומואב urge נבוכדנצר to attack, and this sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמון ומואב used Israel's own נביאים as their reason: if the prophets say ירושלים will fall, now is the time. This begins a series of messages between them and נבוכדנצר.

keyTerms.meaning: Neighboring nations east of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב שִׁיבָבֵי בִּישֵׁי דִּירוּשְׁלֶם הֲווֹ.
phrases.english: Ammon and Moab were bad neighbors of Jerusalem.
Once they heard the prophets
who were prophesying the destruction of Jerusalem,
they sent to Nebuchadnezzar: Go out and come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב שִׁיבָבֵי בִּישֵׁי דִּירוּשְׁלֶם הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related story about נבוכדנצר and the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמון ומואב pushed נבוכדנצר to attack ירושלים.

steps.title: נבוכדנצר is afraid
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר says he fears ending up like earlier attackers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I am afraid that they will do to me what they did to those before me.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר refuses at first because earlier enemies of Israel were defeated. This fear is what עמון ומואב will now try to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kings before him, like סנחריב, attacked ירושלים and fell. His fear sets up the debate: עמון ומואב must convince him that Israel is no longer protected.

keyTerms.meaning: The earlier ones, those before me

phrases.english: He said: I am afraid
that they may do to me
what they did to the earlier ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the invitation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the invitation to attack ירושלים now
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Earlier attackers of ירושלים, like סנחריב, were struck down, so attacking is dangerous

steps.title: The Man is not at home
steps.stepSummary: עמון ומואב quote 'the man is not at home', reading 'man' as ה׳: He has left.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: 'For the man is not at home, he has gone on a far journey.' And 'man' means only הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says: 'ה׳ is a man of war.'
steps.whatsHappening: עמון ומואב answer his fear with a פסוק from משלי: Israel's Protector has left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read 'the man' as ה׳, using the פסוק‎ 'ה׳ is a man of war.' So their argument is that ה׳ is not protecting His house right now.

phrases.english: They sent to him:
"For the man is not at home,
phrases.notes: משלי 7:19

phrases.english: he has gone on a far journey,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אִישׁ אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: and 'man' means only the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it says: "ה׳ is a man of war."
phrases.notes: שמות 15:3

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ: כִּי אֵין הָאִישׁ בְּבֵיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers נבוכדנצר's fear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why should נבוכדנצר not fear Israel's protection?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳, the 'man' of the house, has left.

steps.title: He is nearby and will return
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר replies that ה׳ is close and could come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: He is nearby, and He will come.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר pushes back: even if ה׳ left, He is close and could return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He accepts their reading but says it is not enough. A short absence does not make it safe to attack.

phrases.english: He sent to them: He is nearby, and He will come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 24 as not enough.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial: accepts that ה׳ left, but denies it is safe.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ה׳ might be close by and come back.

steps.title: He went far away
steps.stepSummary: They point to the words 'from afar' in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: 'He has gone on a journey from afar.'
steps.whatsHappening: עמון ומואב answer that the פסוק itself says He went far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They use the second half of the same פסוק. The word 'מרחוק' answers the claim that He is nearby.

phrases.english: They sent to him: "He has gone on a journey from afar."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers נבוכדנצר's objection in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק says He went far away, not nearby.

steps.title: The righteous will pray and bring Him back
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר says Israel has צדיקים whose prayers can bring ה׳ back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: They have righteous people who pray for mercy and bring Him back.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר raises a new worry: Israel's צדיקים can pray and bring ה׳ back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if ה׳ is far away, distance does not matter if צדיקים can call Him back. This sets up the final answer of עמון ומואב.

phrases.english: He sent to them:
They have righteous people
who pray for mercy and bring Him back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 26 by raising the power of the צדיקים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial: accepts that ה׳ is far, but says He can be brought back.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The צדיקים' prayers can bring ה׳ back.

steps.title: He took the righteous with Him
steps.stepSummary: They quote 'He took the bundle of silver with him', with 'silver' meaning צדיקים, proven from הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: 'He took the bundle of silver in his hand.' And 'silver' means only צדיקים, as it says: 'So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a חומר of barley and a לתך of barley.'
steps.whatsHappening: עמון ומואב answer that ה׳ took the צדיקים with Him, so nobody is left to pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read the next פסוק in משלי, where the 'silver' stands for צדיקים. The proof is from הושע, where 'silver' is the price ה׳ paid to acquire Israel. This answers נבוכדנצר's last worry from step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: Measures of barley (a לתך is half a חומר)

phrases.english: They sent to him:
"He took the bundle of silver in his hand,"
phrases.notes: משלי 7:20

phrases.english: and 'silver' means only the righteous,
as it says:
"So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver
phrases.notes: הושע 3:2

phrases.english: and a chomer of barley and a lesech of barley."

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ: צְרוֹר הַכֶּסֶף לָקַח בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry about the צדיקים in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ took the צדיקים ('silver') with Him, so none are left to pray.

steps.title: Maybe the wicked will repent and bring ה׳ back
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר raises a new worry: even if the צדיקים are gone, the wicked might do תשובה and pray, bringing ה׳ back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: The wicked may return in תשובה, pray for mercy, and bring Him back.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר pushes back again. Even with the צדיקים gone, the remaining wicked people could repent and pray for ה׳ to return.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, עמון ומואב said the צדיקים were taken away. נבוכדנצר answers that the wicked can become righteous through תשובה, so the danger is still there.

phrases.english: He sent to them: The wicked may return in repentance,
phrases.notes: 'He' is נבוכדנצר, and 'them' is עמון ומואב.

phrases.english: and pray for mercy and bring Him back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim from step 28 that taking away the צדיקים removed the danger
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Says the absence of צדיקים is not enough to make the attack safe
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wicked can repent and pray, which could also bring ה׳ back

steps.title: ה׳ already set a fixed time
steps.stepSummary: עמון ומואב answer that ה׳ has already set a time for His return, so prayers will not bring Him back early. They prove that 'כסא' means a set time.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: He already set a time for them, as it says 'On the day of the כסא He will come home.' 'כסא' means a set time, as it says 'at the כסה on the day of our feast.'
steps.whatsHappening: עמון ומואב answer that a fixed date has already been set for ה׳'s return. Until then, nothing will change, so נבוכדנצר is free to act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They continue reading the פסוק from משלי about the 'man' who left home: he comes back only 'on the day of the כסא.' To show that 'כסא' means a fixed time, they bring a פסוק from תהלים about a festival day. So repentance will not bring ה׳ back before that time.

keyTerms.meaning: He set a fixed time for them
'This word means only...', a way of defining a word

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ: כְּבָר קָבַע לָהֶן זְמַן,
phrases.english: They sent to him: He already set a time for them,
as it says: 'On the day of the keseh, he will come home.'
phrases.notes: משלי 7:20, the same פסוק as "the bundle of silver." It is still about the man who left home.

phrases.english: 'Keseh' means nothing other than a set time,
as it says: 'At the keseh, on the day of our feast.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 81:4

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ: כְּבָר קָבַע לָהֶן זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers נבוכדנצר's worry about תשובה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳'s return is fixed to a set time, so prayer and repentance will not bring Him back sooner

steps.title: It is winter and I cannot come
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר now gives a practical excuse: it is winter, and snow and rain block the way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: It is winter, and I cannot come because of the snow and the rain.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר stops arguing about ה׳ and gives a practical excuse instead: bad winter weather makes the trip impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spiritual objections have all been answered, so his reason for holding back changes to the physical journey. Snow and rain would make it too hard to bring an army.

phrases.english: He sent to them: It is winter,
and I am not able to come
because of the snow and because of the rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the spiritual concern is answered, raises a practical obstacle
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Pushes back on the plan to come now
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Winter weather makes the trip impossible

steps.title: Come by way of the mountain peaks
steps.stepSummary: עמון ומואב tell him to travel along the mountain tops, and they support this with a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: Come on the peaks of the mountains, as it says: 'Send the lamb to the ruler of the land, from the rock of the wilderness to the mount of the daughter of ציון.'
steps.whatsHappening: עמון ומואב solve the weather problem by telling him to travel along the high mountain route.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read the פסוק as describing a path 'from the rock' (high places) all the way to הר ציון. So there is a route that the winter weather does not block.

keyTerms.meaning: On the peaks of the mountain

phrases.english: They sent to him: Come on the peaks of the mountain,
as it says: 'Send the lamb to the ruler of the land
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 16:1

phrases.aramaic: מִסֶּלַע מִדְבָּרָה אֶל הַר בַּת צִיּוֹן״.
phrases.english: from the rock of the wilderness to the mount of the daughter of Zion.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the winter excuse
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Travel along the mountain tops, a route shown in the פסוק

steps.title: I will have nowhere to stay
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר gives another practical excuse: if he comes, there will be no place for him to stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: If I come, I have no place to stay.
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר raises one more practical problem: where would he and his army stay near ירושלים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The route problem is solved, so his excuse moves to lodging during a long siege. Without a place to stay, the attack is not practical.

phrases.english: He sent to them: If I come,
I have no place to stay in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the route problem is solved, raises the problem of lodging
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There would be no place to stay

steps.title: Their burial caves are finer than your palaces
steps.stepSummary: עמון ומואב answer that the Jewish burial caves are nicer than his palaces. A פסוק in ירמיהו says the bones will be taken out of their graves.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent to him: Their graves are finer than your palaces, as it is written: 'At that time, says ה׳, they will take out the bones of the kings of יהודה, his officers, the כהנים, the נביאים and the people of ירושלים from their graves, and spread them before the sun, the moon and all the hosts of heaven, which they loved, served and followed.'
steps.whatsHappening: עמון ומואב give their final answer: empty out the burial caves and live in them, since they are better than his palaces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the פסוק saying the bones will be taken out of the graves. That shows the graves will be emptied, and so they can be used as a place to stay. With this, every excuse נבוכדנצר raised has been answered.
steps.whatToRemember: נבוכדנצר kept finding reasons not to attack: ה׳ may return, the צדיקים may pray, the wicked may repent, the weather, and lodging. עמון ומואב answered each one with a פסוק.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Empty the burial caves, as the פסוק describes, and stay in them

steps.title: When will 'בר נפלי' come?
steps.stepSummary: A new section begins. רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק whether he has heard when 'בר נפלי' will come.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רבי יצחק: Have you heard when בר נפלי will come?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא starts a new topic. רב נחמן asks a question that opens the discussion about when משיח will come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן uses an unusual name, 'בר נפלי'. This sets up the next few steps, where רבי יצחק first asks what the name means.

keyTerms.meaning: A name for משיח, explained in the next steps

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak:
Have you heard
when Bar Nafli will come?
phrases.notes: Literally 'son of the fallen ones.' The next steps explain why this name is used.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story ends

steps.title: Who is 'בר נפלי'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק does not recognize the name and asks who 'בר נפלי' is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who is בר נפלי?
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, רבי יצחק asks what the strange name means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This clarifying question pauses the main question, 'when?', until the name is explained.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who is Bar Nafli?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the name in the question means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the name בר נפלי refers to

steps.title: It means משיח
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that 'בר נפלי' is משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains that the name refers to משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question is clear: he was asking when משיח will come. But calling משיח by this name still needs a reason, which the next step asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: The anointed king who will redeem Israel

phrases.english: He said to him: The Messiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about who בר נפלי is

steps.title: Why call משיח by that name?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק is surprised and asks whether he really calls משיח 'בר נפלי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You call משיח 'בר נפלי'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק is surprised that משיח would be called by a name that sounds like 'son of the fallen ones,' and asks if that is really what he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the name, not about משיח himself. It sets up רב נחמן to bring a source for the name.

phrases.english: You call the Messiah 'Bar Nafli'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the name given in the answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why משיח is called by this name

steps.title: Yes, there is a פסוק for it
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says yes and begins quoting a פסוק that supports the name.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, as it is written: 'On that day I will raise up...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן confirms the name and starts bringing a פסוק to back it up. The פסוק continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof will connect the name to something 'fallen' in the פסוק. Only the opening words are quoted here.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
as it is written: 'On that day I will raise up
phrases.notes: עמוס 9:11. The rest of the פסוק comes on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, דִּכְתִיב ״בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא אָקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source in answer to the question about the name
steps.raayaObject: That משיח is called בר נפלי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא אָקִים', which continues on the next part of the daf
